races.title: State Senate, District 15
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: Jay J. Chaudhuri
cands.bio: Democratic member of the North Carolina Senate since his April 2016 appointment, now representing District 15. His campaign site says he is Senate Democratic Minority Whip. Earlier he was general counsel and senior policy advisor to State Treasurer Janet Cowell and special counsel to Attorney General Roy Cooper.

endorsements.text: Sierra Club North Carolina is listed by Ballotpedia as endorsing him in 2026.

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was born or when his family settled in North Carolina. His campaign site says he grew up in Fayetteville. We found no documented stance from him on data centers, residential development or growth limits. We found nothing on homestead property tax relief, limits on institutional or foreign buyers of land, H-1B visas, E-Verify or immigration enforcement. We found nothing on police pay or pensions, school vouchers or charters. The pages we reviewed describe his actions mostly through his own campaign site, and we could not confirm those claims against official legislative records. No controversies or foreign ties turned up in these sources.

local.label: Roots 90: His campaign site says he is the son of Indian immigrants who settled in Fayetteville and a product of Cumberland County public schools, so he was raised in North Carolina; his birthplace is not stated.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Ten years in the state Senate (appointed April 2016) and, per his campaign site, three terms as Senate Democratic Minority Whip. Before that he was general counsel and senior policy advisor to the State Treasurer and special counsel to the Attorney General.
qual.why: Long legislative service and caucus leadership, plus a law and policy career in state government, fit the high band for writing law and the state budget. Ballotpedia also lists him on Senate Appropriations and Finance committees, but committee seats were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: Long legislative service and caucus leadership, plus a law and policy career in state government, fit the high band for writing law and the state budget. Ballotpedia also lists him on Senate Appropriations and Finance committees, but committee seats were not counted toward the score.

second-amendment.evidence: His campaign site says he introduced a gun-safety package after the Parkland shooting that would create Extreme Risk Protection Orders, extend background checks to all firearms, raise the minimum age for assault weapon purchases to 21 and ban bump stocks.

pro-life.evidence: His campaign site says he helped lead the committee and Senate floor fight against the 2023 abortion bill, including a six-hour floor debate, and calls the bill government overreach.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: In his 2016 campaign themes he pledged to raise teacher salaries above the national average.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 3 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised

roots.summary: His campaign site says he is the son of Indian immigrants who settled in Fayetteville and a product of Cumberland County public schools, so he was raised in North Carolina; his birthplace is not stated.

cands.name: David Bankert
cands.bio: David Bankert is a retired electrical engineer with a 35-year business career in engineering, manufacturing and construction. He holds a Carnegie Mellon degree and a University of Pittsburgh graduate degree. He has not held public office. He ran for NC Senate in 2022 (District 13), 2024 and 2026 (District 15).

endorsements.text: Listed by Ballotpedia as receiving a 2026 voter guide recommendation from Emily's Picks (Sway voting group by Emily Ellis).

cands.gaps: We could not find where he was raised, where he lived or worked in North Carolina, or the year he moved here. His employers and job titles are not named, so his level of management responsibility is unknown. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2024 or 2026 candidate surveys. We found no documented positions or actions from him on data centers, property taxes, foreign or investor land buying, growth and land conservation, immigration or H-1B, policing, gun laws or school choice. His campaign site lists general themes such as bringing manufacturing back, election integrity and mental health policy, but takes no stance on these topics. We found no news coverage, controversies or foreign ties.

local.label: Roots 55: He was born in Pittsburgh and earned his degrees there in 1978 and 1982, then says on his campaign site that he has lived in North Carolina for more than 35 years, which means he arrived as an adult.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He reports a 35-year business career in engineering, manufacturing and construction, with an electrical engineering degree and an MBA. Ballotpedia also lists computer programming and data work. He has held no elected office.
qual.why: He has a long business and engineering career and a business degree, but no legislative, policy or budget work and no elected office. The pages do not say whether he managed or owned a business.
qual.label: He has a long business and engineering career and a business degree, but no legislative, policy or budget work and no elected office. The pages do not say whether he managed or owned a business.

pro-life.evidence: In his 2022 Ballotpedia survey he said he was adopted and "infinitely favor[s] adoption over abortion." He did not describe any specific abortion law he would support.

prio.label: Matches 1 of 1 priorities; 0 backed by their record, 1 only promised (needs 2 to score)

roots.summary: He was born in Pittsburgh and earned his degrees there in 1978 and 1982, then says on his campaign site that he has lived in North Carolina for more than 35 years, which means he arrived as an adult.
